title: New SSH sign-ins fail after an authentication change
scenario: BR1 is reachable by SSH and a privileged console session remains open. A change selected local AAA for the VTY lines, but the complete relevant configuration contains no local username. These are representative records.

exhibits.title: Current authentication
exhibits.text:
aaa new-model
aaa authentication login default local
line vty 0 4
 login authentication default
 transport input ssh
No username entries

exhibits.title: Observed test
exhibits.text: Fresh SSH reaches authentication and no submitted local account is accepted.

question: Which missing dependency explains the selected method’s failure?
options: Add a central server even though the selected method is local.
Create a valid account for the explicitly selected local method.
Change only the line password while continuing to select local usernames.
Add EXEC accounting and expect it to supply the missing login identity.
explanation: The line selects the local username method and the complete configuration contains no such account. A server definition, line password or accounting list does not populate that database. Correct the local identity through the retained console, then test a new VTY session and console recovery before saving.
fix:
In the disposable lab, from the retained privileged console:
```ios
BR1# configure terminal
BR1(config)# username recovery privilege 15 secret Lab-Recovery-2026!
BR1(config)# aaa authentication login CONSOLE local
BR1(config)# line console 0
BR1(config-line)# login authentication CONSOLE
BR1(config-line)# end
```
Test a fresh recovery SSH login. Keep it open while verifying a fresh console login, then inspect every VTY range and save the intended configuration. Replace public examples with approved unique secrets outside a disposable lab.

title: The central service sees no requests during SSH sign-ins
scenario: R2 has one TACACS+ server TAC1 in MGMT-TAC. A controlled new SSH login uses a local account instantly. The central service sees no request and the device’s request counter does not increase. The complete VTY configuration for this test is shown.

exhibits.title: Definitions and methods
exhibits.text:
tacacs server TAC1
 address ipv4 10.0.0.100
 key [omitted]
aaa group server tacacs+ MGMT-TAC
 server name TAC1
aaa authentication login default local
aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group MGMT-TAC local

exhibits.title: Actual selected VTY configuration
exhibits.text:
line vty 0 4
 login authentication default
 transport input ssh

question: Which configuration change selects the intended central-first login policy?
options: Bind login authentication VTY-AUTH to the intended VTY range.
Change the central account password before selecting its method list.
Add the same reachable server to a second unused group.
Change only the default list while assuming the explicitly named VTY list is already selected.
explanation: The VTY explicitly selects default, which is local-only. The central-first VTY-AUTH list exists but does not participate. Binding that intended list preserves the separate local default and console policy; changing credentials or an unused group would not select it. Replacing the default list would change the scope of other users of default rather than implement the specified named binding.
fix:
Keep the tested local console session open:
```ios
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# line vty 0 4
R2(config-line)# login authentication VTY-AUTH
R2(config-line)# end
```
Apply the intended binding to any additional existing VTY ranges. Test a fresh central success, explicit rejection, and controlled ERROR fallback while keeping console recovery. Save only after those results match policy.
